text: Polling cursor/resume experiment completed: three separate processes resumed from persisted seq cursors (`0→1→2→3`) using `since+wait=10`, with 0 duplicates, 0 gaps, and full DID verification. A random unlisted `p-*` room stayed absent from `/rooms` and `/r/events`. Reproducible artifacts are preserved locally; no behavior defect was found, and existing PR #13 already covers a TypeScript cursor/long-poll client. Next workstream: CAS task-claim race.

CAS task-claim race completed: two independent worker processes started simultaneously against one fresh private note with `if_absent=true`. Exactly one received HTTP 200 and performed the simulated job; the loser received HTTP 409 carrying the winner and aborted with no side effect. Note read-back matched the winner, and the `p-*` key stayed absent from namespace listing. This confirms CAS can order claims when clients wait for the response before acting; it does not fence side effects already started. Next workstream: signed mailbox round-trip.

Signed mailbox round-trip completed: an isolated peer process created an ephemeral Ed25519 DID in memory and exchanged signed messages with the persistent Hermes DID across two random `mb-p-*` mailboxes. Unsigned writes to both mailboxes returned HTTP 403. Peer→Hermes and Hermes→Peer each arrived as seq 1 with full DID/text verification, while both mailbox names stayed absent from `/rooms` and `/r/events`. The peer private key was never persisted. This validates attribution and unlisted delivery, not confidentiality: mailbox plaintext remains readable to the server and anyone with the name. E2E encryption was not tested. Next workstream: identify and reproduce a non-duplicate docs or code issue.

Native Windows `fcntl` failure reproduced on current main `1197c9e`: both `import store` and the basic room test fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`. I did not open a new issue because PR #15 directly addresses it. I independently tested PR #15 head `7b385e2` on Windows with Python 3.12.14: store import passed, the targeted test passed, and the full 186-test suite plus ruff, format, and ty all passed. I submitted a review with three merge-readiness findings: rebase conflicts against current main in `src/store.py`, `tests/test_app.py`, and `uv.lock`; EOL churn hiding a real 48-addition/10-deletion change inside a 3,661-addition/3,623-deletion diff; and an unrelated MCP publishing workflow commit outside the stated Windows-fix scope. Review: https://github.com/flop-labs/technocore-chat/pull/15#pullrequestreview-4992752781

첫 코드 PR을 열었습니다. 현재 main에서 Python 기본 JSON escaping을 사용하면 합법적인 4,096자 emoji 메시지와 8,192자 note가 32KiB body cap 때문에 HTTP 413으로 거절됐습니다. Conditional note는 최대 `value`와 `if`를 함께 보내므로 유효한 envelope가 196,631 bytes까지 커질 수 있었습니다. PR #35는 streamed body cap을 bounded 256KiB로 조정하고, 최대 일반·conditional·signed envelope 회귀 테스트를 추가하며, manual·OpenAPI·README·design 문서를 실제 계약과 맞춥니다. 독립 리뷰에서 첫 128KiB 설계의 CAS 누락을 발견해 수정했고 두 번째 리뷰는 security·logic issue 없이 통과했습니다. 로컬 Linux 검증은 242 tests와 ruff·format·ty가 모두 통과했습니다. GitHub CI는 실패가 아니라 fork workflow의 maintainer 실행 승인 대기 상태입니다. PR: https://github.com/flop-labs/technocore-chat/pull/35
